**Internal Hackathon**

**(Smart India Hackathon 2026\)**

Organised by: Keshav Mahavidyalaya, University of Delhi

**Round-1 (Online): Mock Presentation / Prelims Screening**  
Date: 3rd–4th September, 2026   |   Venue: Online (Google Meet)

**Round-2 (Offline): Internal Hackathon**  
Date: 10th September, 2026   |   Venue: Reading Room

**Overview**

Keshav Mahavidyalaya successfully conducted the Internal Hackathon under Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2026 in two structured parts. The first part, held online on 3–4 September 2026, served as a mock-presentation and prelims screening round in which teams presented their proposed solutions to shortlisted problem statements before a faculty panel via Google Meet. The second part, the offline internal hackathon, was conducted on 10 September 2026 in the Reading Room, where nominated teams presented refined solutions for final evaluation. The exercise gave students a structured platform to ideate, prototype and pitch solutions in a manner closely aligned with the format of the national-level SIH.

**Event Highlights**

* Cross-functional student teams registered and participated, with 21 teams comprising 126 participants (79 male, 46 female, 1 unspecified) taking part in the online prelims.  
* The online round consisted of mock presentations enabling teams to screen and validate their problem-statement ideas before a faculty panel.  
* Based on the online screening, 19 teams comprising 114 participants (71 male, 42 female, 1 unspecified) were nominated to the offline internal hackathon.  
* The offline round, held on campus on 10 September 2026 in the Reading Room, saw all 19 nominated teams present their solutions for final evaluation.  
* Ideas were screened and evaluated by a panel of faculty judges against a prescribed set of criteria totalling 100 marks.

**Judging Process**

The evaluation was conducted in two stages. In the online mock-presentation round on 3–4 September 2026, all 21 teams presented their proposed solutions over Google Meet, following which 19 teams were nominated to proceed to the offline internal hackathon. In the offline round on 10 September 2026, each of the 19 nominated teams presented its solution before a panel of faculty judges drawn from the Departments of Computer Science, Mathematics and Management Studies. Teams were assessed on a 100-mark rubric comprising:

* Idea & Innovation (20 marks)  
* Problem Alignment & Complexity (10 marks)  
* Technical Feasibility (15 marks)  
* Practicability (15 marks)  
* Impact, Scalability & Sustainability (20 marks)  
* Clarity & Presentation (20 marks)

**Total: 100 marks**

**Outcome**

Following evaluation of all 19 nominated teams, the best-performing ideas were identified for recognition. HEXCODE and Team Tiramisu jointly led the standings with 87 marks each, followed closely by Trinetra (85), and Embiot and 64 Bits (84 each). The rankings reflect the strength of ideation and presentation demonstrated across the participating teams, with the top performers set to represent Keshav Mahavidyalaya in the subsequent stages of Smart India Hackathon 2026\.

**Jury Details**

The jury members for the internal hackathon were:

**Prof. Anjali Thukral**  
An Associate Professor in the Department of Computer Science at Keshav Mahavidyalaya, University of Delhi. With over 25 years of teaching experience, she obtained her PhD in Computer Science from the University of Delhi in 2013\. She has numerous publications in international journals and conferences and has authored book chapters. Her research interests include information retrieval, knowledge representation and reasoning using ontology, knowledge graphs and semantic web technologies, particularly in e-learning and disease diagnosis systems.

**Prof. Richa Sharma**  
Professor with over 27 years of teaching experience. She has extensive publications in e-learning systems and computational intelligence. Her research interests include Natural Language Processing, Sentiment Analysis, Data Science, Machine Learning, Knowledge Management, Collaborative Learning, Social Opinion Modeling, e-Learning Systems and Intelligent Information Systems.

**Prof. Bhavna Gupta**  
An Associate Professor in the Department of Computer Science, Keshav Mahavidyalaya, University of Delhi. She did her doctorate in Computer Science from the University of Delhi in 2014 and has over 24 years of teaching experience. She has published research papers in international journals and conferences. Her interests include Artificial Intelligence, Multi-Agent Systems, trust-based recommender systems, Information Retrieval, Cloud Computing and AI in Healthcare and Natural Language Processing.
